clue.text: Plucky female has no appreciation of music

parts.note: to have an ear for music is to appreciate it
the suffix -less means lacking or having none

explanation.surface: A brave woman confesses she is tone-deaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone plucky shows courage and is unafraid of danger.

clue.text: In appearance the Italian is slick

indicators.note: In shows one word is set inside another

parts.note: face means outward appearance, as in on the face of it
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: The Italian man looks smooth and polished.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile means glib and superficial, like a slick answer.

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: an auberge is a French inn
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A dish is a favourite at a French inn.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine, or eggplant, is a purple fruit eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Write .1 not 0.1 to give a complete picture

definitions.meaning: writing .1 drops the zero, the nought or nothing, from 0.1
an idiom for including every detail

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads literally: omit the 0, which is 'nothing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit no detail is to include everything and tell the whole story.

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, read backwards
involving means the first word takes in the second

parts.note: rows, rhyming with cows, are loud noises
a bob was a British shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: Arguments about a boy cause a meeting to be disrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts S inside NOISES, and 'upset' turns NOISSES backwards. 'Rows' rhymes with cows here, not lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A session is a sitting or meeting of a body such as a court or council.

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the whole run of letters the other way

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a student
warps means bends or twists out of shape

explanation.surface: A student fidgets and squirms while sitting in the common room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns L + WARPS (LWARPS) backwards. 'lounge' looks like a room but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to stretch out lazily, the same idea as lying spread out.

clue.text: Became late having left footwear at uncle's

definitions.meaning: late means dead, so this is to die
uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker; to pop something is to pawn it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Popped one's clogs' is a British idiom for died; the second reading takes it literally, pawning one's shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular British idiom for dying.

parts.note: a miss is a young girl

explanation.surface: A young woman is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrong or awry, as in something is amiss.

indicators.note: worn round means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: lint is a fabric used for dressing wounds
a game leg is an injured or lame one

explanation.surface: A bandage is wrapped around an injured sinew.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is fibrous connective tissue, loosely a sinew like a tendon.

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

explanation.surface: A plotter from the USA is described as humourless.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was one of the plotters who assassinated Julius Caesar.

parts.note: Co. is the short form of company, a firm
a bra is an undergarment that supports

explanation.surface: Someone sycophantic is described as a staunch backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake is a reptile that crawls along the ground; the cobra is one example.

indicators.note: in tells us one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm
to trip is to stumble and fall

explanation.surface: A young person takes a tumble and ends up with an arm in a sling.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is an adolescent lad, a young man.

indicators.note: knocked off suggests the letters have been battered into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone has stolen a set of woodwind instruments from a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked off' is slang for stolen, adding to the theft picture while signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft, so one who commits it is a robber.

clue.text: Track in record having remarkable cut

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: some can mean remarkable, as in that was some show

explanation.surface: A song on an extended-play disc has a striking edit.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is a famous English racecourse, home of the Derby; 'Track' looks musical given 'record'.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a horse-racing course in Surrey.

clue.text: Cast off melancholy when touring Iceland

indicators.note: touring means going all the way around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: feeling down is feeling sad
IS is the international vehicle code for Iceland

explanation.surface: A gloomy traveller in Iceland sheds their cares.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast someone off is to reject them and refuse to acknowledge them.

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: shown, as in shown the way, means guided
MA is the international code for Morocco

explanation.surface: A theatrical producer was taken on a tour of Morocco.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario is a theatrical promoter, a person who puts on spectacles.

clue.text: Artisan seeing a feature in the fog

indicators.note: in tells us the pair goes inside the other word

parts.note: mist is a light fog
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A craftsman glimpses a shape looming out of the haze.
explanation.definitionFit: A machinist is a skilled worker who operates machine tools.

indicators.note: upset suggests these letters are overturned and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A timid man is distressed by a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sealyham is a small white Welsh terrier breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sealyham terrier is a breed of dog from Wales.

indicators.note: could be suggests the word may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: An ideal society may not exist anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Butler's satirical novel named its imaginary land by rearranging 'nowhere', echoing that utopia means 'no place'.
explanation.definitionFit: Butler's fictional country is a satirical ideal land, like Thomas More's.

indicators.note: fermented suggests the letters are stirred and agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek islander brews an alcoholic beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the gods in Greek myth, and any delicious beverage.

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated p
to reach someone is to contact or get hold of them

explanation.surface: Police officers obtain someone's home details.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a congregation is to deliver a sermon or speech to it.

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for or covet it
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone envies a lady's pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The panther is a big cat, a leopard or puma.

clue.text: Biddy introduced to one Greek goddess or another

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside the following word

parts.note: Ate was the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin
biddy is an old word for a hen

explanation.surface: An old woman meets several deities of ancient Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biddy' looks like an old woman but is a hen. The definition is just 'another' Greek goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, or Athena, is the Greek goddess of wisdom, a second deity alongside Ate.

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: Someone was billed for a French course.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or burdened, as a charged vessel is filled.

clue.text: Addict has a short period in hide-out

indicators.note: in shows one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a den is a lair or hiding place
a mo is a moment

explanation.surface: A drug user spends a brief time in a secret lair.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon for something is an enthusiast or fiend for it, as an addict is.

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
script means handwriting, and calligraphy is fine handwriting

explanation.surface: An inmate wows people with beautiful penmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impress' here is the old sense of forcing men into military service, as a press gang did.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to force into service; a conscript is someone enlisted compulsorily, used here as a verb.

clue.text: Medic gets orchestra leader in the family way

indicators.note: in places the one letter inside the joined words

parts.note: home stands for one's family and household
a path is a way

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A doctor finds the conductor's wife is pregnant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface leans on 'in the family way', an idiom for pregnant; the phrase must be split, with 'the' only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A homeopath practises an alternative form of medicine, so is loosely a doctor.

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means one word surrounds the other

parts.note: one means a person, as in one should
pi is the ratio, a fixed relationship, of a circle's circumference to its diameter

explanation.surface: A judge is described as someone single and unattached.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge here is to give a view, to express an opinion.

clue.text: Greek character interrupts child for a time

indicators.note: interrupts means one word breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: a mite is a small child
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person briefly disturbs a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is a short span of sixty seconds.

clue.text: French working girl stuck in Tigre, sadly

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters are in a sorry, jumbled state

parts.note: set means fixed, stuck in place

explanation.surface: A young woman from France is miserably marooned in a Spanish river region.
explanation.walkthrough: SET (stuck) and TIGRE together are rearranged. A grisette was a young French working-class woman, often a seamstress.
explanation.definitionFit: A grisette was a Parisian shop girl or seamstress, named for her grey dress.
